body:
# Hāḇel: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Hāḇel** stay *habel*.

Hāḇel's mythology is almost entirely passive. He does not choose his fate; he is chosen by God's favor and killed by his brother's envy. In that passivity, however, he becomes one of the most powerful symbols in the biblical tradition. Cain and Abel both bring offerings to the LORD.  Cain brings fruit of the ground; Abel brings the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Hāḇel
- **ASCII form:** habel
- **Meaning:** "Second son of Adam and Eve"
- **Domain of influence:** First Victim
- **Pantheon:** Canaanite
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** הֶבֶל
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 2 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Hāḇel** to *habel* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Macron: long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Hāḇel** lives at [/sites/abel/](/sites/abel/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/abel/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/abel/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/abel/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Hāḇel** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — The accepted offering; faith’s first martyr.
- **Funerary & Memorial Services** — The first death and the first grave; mourning begins at his field.
- **Mental Health & Emotional Wellness** — The vulnerable self destroyed by envy; the Abel-figure of every psychology of violence.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Canaanite tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Enūma Eliš](/texts/enuma-elish/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/abel/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Ꜣb** ([read it here](/sites/ab/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Achérōn** ([read it here](/sites/acheron/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
